newsitem.title: ITALY: UN agency says food stocks looted in Sierra Leone.
newsitem.headline: UN agency says food stocks looted in Sierra Leone.

text.p: Looters pillaged the U.N. World Food Programme's warehouses in the capital of Sierra Leone and stole 1,650 tonnes of food aid in violence following last weekend's military coup, the agency said on Tuesday.

The Rome-based agency, which runs United Nations food aid programmes, said staff houses and port facilities in Freetown had also been ransacked after Major Johnny Paul Koromah ousted the elected government last Sunday.
"Looters ransacked the homes of U.N. staff and WFP port installations, stealing some 1,650 tonnes of food, 15 light vehicles and trucks," the WFP said in a statement.
None of its staff was injured in the violence.
The U.N. agency launched a $19.4 million food aid operation for Sierra Leone early this year to encourage the resettlement of thousands of people displaced by six years of civil war.
It said the renewed violence would hamper its ability to continue aid operations in the impoverished West African state.

"WFP expresses concern that the breakdown of order and loss of stocks and equipment will seriously complicate its efforts to distribute food aid to women, children and other members of vulnerable groups in Freetown," the statement said.
Koromah said he had overthrown the elected government of president Ahmad Tejan Kabbah because his one-year administration had failed to consolidate peace.
